falling-asleep-easily.title: Falling asleep soon after I go to bed
falling-asleep-easily.line: Most nights I get into bed, put the light out, and I'm asleep before I've had time to start worrying.
falling-asleep-easily.writerNotes: Sleep onset. Why: so I'm not lying awake, which is the pain itself, so this is the end state. Swap: falling asleep only belongs to sleep, not to Energy or Burnout. Distinct from staying asleep and from waking early: it's the start of the night.

sleeping-through-the-night.title: Sleeping through the night without waking
sleeping-through-the-night.line: Most nights I sleep straight through from when I drop off until morning.
sleeping-through-the-night.writerNotes: Sleep maintenance, the guide's own example. Why: so the night isn't broken, which is the pain. Swap: specific to sleep. Distinct from getting back to sleep (which accepts waking) and from early waking (the end of the night).

back-to-sleep-quickly.title: Getting back to sleep quickly when I wake
back-to-sleep-quickly.line: If I wake at 3 in the morning, I roll over and I'm asleep again in a few minutes, not lying there until dawn.
back-to-sleep-quickly.writerNotes: For people who will always wake now and then (age, kids, a bathroom trip) the end state is that waking costs nothing. Why: so the night stays whole; still the pain, so it's an end state, not a means. Swap: sleep only. Flagged as overlapping with sleeping through the night.

sleeping-until-morning.title: Sleeping until it's time to get up
sleeping-until-morning.line: I sleep until my alarm or a little before, not wide awake at 4 in the morning with the day already running through my head.
sleeping-until-morning.writerNotes: Early-morning waking is its own common pattern, often tied to stress or age. Why: to get the last hours of sleep, which is the pain. Swap: specific to sleep. Flagged as overlapping with sleeping through the night.

enough-hours-most-nights.title: Getting enough hours of sleep most nights
enough-hours-most-nights.line: Most nights I get the seven or eight hours I need, instead of getting by on five or six.
enough-hours-most-nights.writerNotes: Quantity rather than quality: for people whose sleep is cut short by work, kids, or late nights rather than insomnia. Why: to feel rested, which is the Energy pain, so this is the top of the ladder for this pain. Swap: hours of sleep don't fit Energy unchanged; Energy is how I feel during the day.

waking-up-rested.title: Waking up feeling like I actually slept
waking-up-rested.line: When I wake up, I feel like the night counted, instead of feeling like I spent eight hours in bed and got nothing from it.
waking-up-rested.writerNotes: Unrefreshing sleep: people who sleep enough hours but wake foggy (light sleep, apnea, light or noise during sleep). Why: so the sleep does its job; still the pain. Swap risk: close to Energy, but it's about the morning after the night, not energy all day; the screen should check it against always-tired. Distinct from enough-hours, which is about quantity.

breathing-easily-asleep.title: Breathing easily all night while I sleep
breathing-easily-asleep.line: I breathe steadily through the night, without snoring loud enough to wake anyone or waking up gasping.
breathing-easily-asleep.writerNotes: The snoring and sleep apnea end state, which the voided draft only reached as a means (knowing whether my snoring is apnea). Why: so my sleep isn't broken and I wake clear-headed, still the pain. Swap: specific to sleep. Flagged as overlapping with waking up rested, since apnea is one cause of unrefreshing sleep.

sleep-at-hours-that-fit.title: Sleeping at hours that fit my life
sleep-at-hours-that-fit.line: My body gets sleepy at a sensible bedtime and wakes when I need it to, instead of being wide awake at two in the morning and dead on my feet at seven.
sleep-at-hours-that-fit.writerNotes: Timing: night owls, shift workers, teens, and people thrown off by clock changes. Why: so I can sleep when my life lets me, which is still the pain. Swap: about the body clock and sleep, so it doesn't fit another pain. Distinct from falling asleep easily, which is about the act of drifting off at any hour.

sleeping-well-without-pills.title: Sleeping well without needing a pill
sleeping-well-without-pills.line: Most nights I drift off and stay asleep with no sleeping pill or nightcap to help me.
sleeping-well-without-pills.writerNotes: For people relying on medication, melatonin, or alcohol, the end state is sleep that doesn't depend on them. Why: a pill is already a way to sleep, so wanting sleep without one is a different end state, not a means. Swap: specific to sleep. Flagged as overlapping with falling asleep easily.

not-worrying-about-sleep.title: Not worrying about sleep anymore
not-worrying-about-sleep.line: I don't count the hours left at night or plan my day around how badly I slept; sleep just happens.
not-worrying-about-sleep.writerNotes: The relationship to sleep: the dread and clock-watching that keep insomnia going. Why: so sleep stops being a problem I manage, which is the pain resolved. Swap: worry about sleep is specific to sleep, not general anxiety. Flagged as overlapping with falling asleep easily.

both-of-us-sleep-well.title: My partner and I both sleeping well
both-of-us-sleep-well.line: My partner and I both get a good night's sleep, and neither of us is the reason the other one is lying awake.
both-of-us-sleep-well.writerNotes: The shared end state for couples where snoring, restlessness, or different hours keep one up. It names no way there (same bed or separate rooms are both fixes). Why: so we both sleep, which is the pain for two people. Swap: specific to sleep. Flagged as overlapping with sleeping through the night.

overlaps.reason: Both describe an unbroken night; one rules out waking and the other only rules out staying awake.
Waking at 4 a.m. and not getting back to sleep is one way of not sleeping through the night.
Dread at bedtime is often what stops someone falling asleep, so the two can read as the same end state.
Falling asleep on my own may already contain falling asleep without a pill.
Interrupted breathing is a main cause of waking unrested, so one may contain the other.
For a couple, both sleeping well may just be each person sleeping through the night.
